params.q: What is the standard deduction for salaried employees under the new tax regime in India?

search_parameters.q: What is the standard deduction for salaried employees under the new tax regime in India?

response.header: Under India’s new tax regime, the standard deduction for salaried employees is ₹75,000 per year.

text_blocks.snippet: Direct answer: All three sources confirm that the standard deduction is ₹75,000 for salaried individuals under the new tax regime, effective from FY 2025–26 onward +2 .

text_blocks.snippet: The higher ₹75,000 deduction is one of the key incentives for choosing the new tax regime, as it directly reduces taxable salary before slab rates apply.

references.title: Standard Deduction ₹75,000 New Tax Regime 2026 | Tax Garden
references.snippet: The standard deduction is capped at Rs 75,000 in total for the year under the new regime, or Rs 50,000 under the old regime, however many employers paid you. If both employers allowed it in their Form 16, report total gross salary in your ITR with a single deduction.

No bill, investment proof or expense voucher is required. The deduction is normally reflected in Form 16 and Schedule Salary ...

references.title: Standard Deduction FY 2026-27 for Salaried Employees | ₹75,000 vs ...
references.snippet: What is Standard Deduction? Standard Deduction under **Section 16 (ia)** of the Income Tax Act is a flat deduction available to all salaried employees and pensioners in India without requiring any bills, receipts, or investment proofs.

references.title: Standard Deduction for Salaried Employees in India 2026 - BankBazaar
references.snippet: The standard deduction that can be claimed by salaried individuals is Rs.75,000 under the new tax regime, effective from FY 2025-26. Earlier, the standard deduction was Rs 75,000, and there has been no change in the old tax regime (as of July 2026) with respect to standard deduction.

references.title: Standard Deduction for Salaried Employees: Current Limits
references.snippet: For FY 2026-27, the standard deduction is Rs 75,000 under the new tax regime and Rs 50,000 under the old tax regime. It applies automatically against salary and pension income under Section 16, with no investment or paperwork required.

references.title: Old Regime vs New Regime for Salaried Employees - Tax Tip
references.snippet: The New Tax Regime is the default for AY 2026-27 and generally works better for salaried employees with few deductions — it now makes taxable income up to ₹12 lakh effectively tax-free (up to roughly ₹12.75 lakh gross salary, after the ₹75,000 standard deduction).

references.title: Standard Deduction for Salaried Individuals in New & Old Tax Regime
references.snippet: Yes, Standard Deduction has been increased from Rs.50,000 to Rs.75,000 only for tax payers opting for new tax regime. This increase is applicable from FY 2024-25.

references.title: Standard Deduction for Salaried Individuals in India - 2025
references.snippet: In Budget 2024, a standard deduction of Rs. 75,000 per year was introduced for salaried individuals who are new income taxpayers. The standard deduction for salaried individuals is a key provision in today’s Indian tax system.

references.title: Standard Deduction Explained for Salaried Employees
references.snippet: The standard deduction is a fixed amount deducted from salary income before tax is worked out. For salaried employees and pensioners in India, the current common figure used for FY 2025-26 is ₹75,000.
